_comment: The research layer's TOOL SURFACE — what an agent sees, by name, for the four plugin research services (evidence, searxng, fetch, edgar). scripts/evidence_proxy.py applies it to every tools/list (live or the cold-start snapshot in research_layer_tools.json, which stays the UPSTREAM listing) and maps every tools/call back to the upstream tool with the entry's preset arguments. An upstream tool with no entry here is NOT exposed. WHY (owner, 2026-10-11): 'For each of the MCP tools, avoid generic names, split by functionality to ensure thorough results, as per gold standard requirements. Ensure clear description of tools' and 'check the gold standard scoring workbook columns eg excerpts, URLs, dates etc.' Names: the full tool name `mcp__plugin_dma-insights_<service>__<name>` must stay within the API's 64 characters (tests/test_research_tool_surface.py). `preset` arguments are fixed by the proxy and removed from the schema the agent sees; `hide` removes further arguments the agent must not set. `appendix` names a shared paragraph from `appendices` appended to the description.

appendices.cards: OUTPUT → GOLD WORKBOOK. Each card is one Evidence_Detail row: register card['item'] UNCHANGED through `engine.cli evidence` (or register_evidence). Source_Name ← item.source_name (publisher and page title, spelled out). Source_URL ← item.source_url (the page the excerpt is on; provenance.url_status 'archived' means an archive copy). Tier ← item.tier (set by the source registry from the URL, never typed by you; the entity's own domain is never T1). Date_Published ← item.published_date: a date the PAGE states, else null — never the retrieval date; null bands the row UNVERIFIED. Claim_Type ← item.claim_type (FACT only on T1/T2, else INFERENCE). SubCap_IDs ← item.linked_subcap_ids (exactly the cell ids you passed for the question the card answered — the engine never invents one). Excerpt ← item.excerpt (verbatim, 50–500 characters, sentence-complete; provenance.excerpt_offsets locate it in the cached page). The ledger then computes E_ID, Fact_ID, ERS, Recency (CURRENT ≤12 months · RECENT ≤24 · DATED ≤36 · STALE ≤48 · ARCHIVAL older · UNVERIFIED undated), Retrieved_At and Access_Status, and appends the E_ID and Source_URL to each cell's Evidence_IDs and Source_URLs on its P*_Subcap_Scoring row. by_question[] with answered=false is that cell's nothing-found material (Proxy_Searched, Negative_Ladder, Proxy_Log); coverage.ladder_searched names the rungs searched. Log the call as one Search_Log row per cell (SubCap_ID, Facet, Query, Tool=evidence_engine, Hits, Kept, Outcome).
appendices.snippets: OUTPUT IS A RESULT LIST, NOT EVIDENCE: each result is a title, a URL and the search engine's snippet. A snippet is a summary the search engine wrote — never register it as an Excerpt and never take a date from it. To cite a result, read the page through `engine.cli fetch --url <url> --query '<cell question>'` (it caches the page so the ledger can verify the span) or ask find_evidence_all_sources for cards. Log each query as a Search_Log row (SubCap_ID, Facet, Query, Tool=searxng, Hits, Kept, Outcome).
appendices.page: OUTPUT IS PAGE TEXT for the servicing tier and the technographic scanner (category researchers and challengers are refused by the deny_whole_page_fetch hook and read through `engine.cli fetch`, whose cached copy is what the ledger verifies an Excerpt against). Take Excerpt as a verbatim 50–500 character, sentence-complete span; take Date_Published only from a date the page itself states (byline, publication metadata, URL path), never the date you read it.
appendices.registry: OUTPUT → GOLD WORKBOOK. A registry record states identity facts, never a judgement: Firmographics rows Regulator (the registry or primary_regulator), Charter or registry identifier (charter number, FDIC certificate, CRD, CIK, UNINUM), Charter type, Headquarters (city and region), Status, and — where the registry states them — Total assets and Members, each with its Unit and As at; registry answers are stated, never held. Cite the match's record_url as the Evidence row's Source_URL (a regulator or filing authority: Tier T1, Claim_Type FACT) after reading the record through `engine.cli fetch`, so the Excerpt is verbatim from the record and Date_Published is the date it states. The identifier is the identity anchor the ET gates check every later source against: a namesake (match_score below 1.0, a different city, `ambiguous`) is not the entity until the record says so. A `candidates` row is a page to open, not a fact.
appendices.sec: SEC EDGAR is the filing authority's copy: a filing or XBRL fact is Tier T1, Claim_Type FACT. For the Evidence_Detail row cite the filing document URL on sec.gov/Archives (Source_URL), name the form and period in Source_Name (e.g. 'Form 10-K for fiscal 2025 — Example Bancorp'), take Date_Published from the filing date, and take a verbatim Excerpt from the filing text; a bare XBRL number is a Firmographics Value with its Unit and As at period, cited to the same filing.

_instructions_comment: Server instructions the proxy returns at initialize in place of the upstream service's, so they name the surfaced tools.

instructions.evidence: Gold-standard evidence cards for DMA research. Call find_evidence_all_sources first — one call per capability, every cell question in `questions`; chase the cells by_question[] leaves unanswered with the per-class find_* tool for the source class the cell's evidence ladder still owes (regulator, trade press, news, job postings, customer reviews, academic) before declaring an absence; stop a facet when coverage.saturation is true; register card['item'] through register_evidence (or engine.cli evidence) unchanged; use expand_card_context only for disambiguation or a challenge; verify_evidence_cards before promotion. The engine never links cells, labels claims beyond the licensed default, or resolves a conflict.

evidence.name: find_evidence_all_sources
evidence.description: PRIMARY research call — run it FIRST for every capability. Batch the whole capability in ONE call: `questions` as objects {"question": "<the cell's diagnostic question>", "subcap_ids": ["P1C1.1.1"], "facet": "primary"}, one per cell question (and one per owed facet — works, fails, value, contradicts, corroborates — naming every cell it bears on). Searches EVERY source class the gold evidence ladder uses — regulator records, SEC filings, trade press, news and wires, the entity's own site, job boards, customer review sites, academic research — through the free SearXNG and Parallel search backends in one pass, fetches one page slice, and returns ranked evidence cards grouped by the cell they answer. `entity`: {legal_name, domains[], aliases[], location, charter, cik, ticker}. `sub_vertical` selects the sector's site pack (credit unions, banks, lending, insurance, wealth). `max_cards`/`token_budget` are per question. A vendor or platform name in a question is refused unless `allow_names_from_cards` maps it to the card it came from (find the estate, never confirm a guess). Follow up the cells `by_question[]` left unanswered with the per-class find_* tools below before declaring an absence.

evidence.name: find_regulator_evidence
evidence.description: Evidence from REGULATOR and government records only: .gov bodies (NCUA, FDIC, OCC, Federal Reserve, SEC, CFPB, FFIEC, state departments of financial institutions), NAIC, FINRA and non-US prudential regulators. Call reports, enforcement and consent orders, examination findings, charter and membership facts, complaint data. Tier T1 (a regulator's own press release T2) — the strongest rung of the evidence ladder, and the 'regulator' rung an absence must show was searched. Use it for governance, compliance, risk and enforcement cells (P1C2, P3C2, P3C3, P3C4), firmographic registry facts (charter, regulator, branches), and every cell find_evidence_all_sources left unanswered. Same `questions` batching as find_evidence_all_sources; only hits that classify as regulator are kept (search.class_filtered counts the rest).

evidence.name: find_trade_press_evidence
evidence.description: Evidence from FINANCIAL-SERVICES TRADE PRESS only, sector pack first: American Banker, Banking Dive, The Financial Brand, CU Times, CUInsight, CreditUnions.com, Insurance Journal, ThinkAdvisor, InvestmentNews, PYMNTS, Fintech Futures, trade associations (America's Credit Unions, ABA, ICBA). Tier T3. Trade press is where a platform deployment, a digital launch, a core conversion or a leadership hire is reported by a third party — the corroboration a T5 vendor case study needs (DQ_Corroborates, Triangulation). Same `questions` batching as find_evidence_all_sources; only trade-press hits are kept.

evidence.name: find_news_wire_evidence
evidence.description: Evidence from NEWS outlets and press-release WIRES only: Reuters, Bloomberg, WSJ, FT, CNBC, AP, PR Newswire, Business Wire, GlobeNewswire. Tier T3 for reporting; a wire copy of the entity's or a vendor's own release is the issuer's words (T5 when the path is a release) and counts as syndication, not as an independent source. Use it for dated events — launches, partnerships, acquisitions, outages, settlements — that feed Entity_Timeline (Event_Date from the article's stated date) and why-now signals. Same `questions` batching as find_evidence_all_sources; only news and wire hits are kept.

evidence.name: find_job_posting_evidence
evidence.description: Evidence from JOB POSTINGS only (the evidence ladder's 'careers' rung): Indeed, Glassdoor, LinkedIn Jobs, Lever, Greenhouse, Workday and iCIMS career sites. Tier T3. A posting shows what the institution is building or staffing NOW — a data team, a cloud migration, a named platform in the required skills — which is the org_talent proxy class for a cell with no direct disclosure. A platform named in a posting supports an INFERENCE (Tech_Register status INFERRED, Detection_Method job_posting), never a CONFIRMED deployment on its own. Applicant-tracking boards (Greenhouse, Lever, Workday, iCIMS) are read and carded; Indeed and LinkedIn pages are found but their robots.txt refuses automated reading, so their postings come through the Indeed connector (search_jobs), not this tool. Same `questions` batching as find_evidence_all_sources; only job-board hits are kept.

evidence.name: find_customer_review_evidence
evidence.description: Evidence from CUSTOMER REVIEW and rating sites only: Apple App Store and Google Play listings, Trustpilot, BBB, WalletHub, Bankrate, NerdWallet, DepositAccounts, G2. Tier T3. This is the member/customer voice — app ratings, recurring complaints, feature gaps — for the experience cells (P2C1–P2C4), the fails facet (DQ_Fails) and the sentiment card; a rating needs its scale, sample size and as-of date from the page. Same `questions` batching as find_evidence_all_sources; only review-site hits are kept.

evidence.name: find_academic_evidence
evidence.description: Evidence from ACADEMIC and economic research only: arXiv, SSRN, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, DOI-resolved papers, NBER. Tier T3. Use it for a sector benchmark, a method or an industry finding that explains WHY a capability matters (Why_It_Matters, DMA_Impact) — rarely for a fact about the entity itself. Same `questions` batching as find_evidence_all_sources; only academic hits are kept.

evidence.name: find_contradicting_evidence
evidence.description: Hunts evidence AGAINST a claim: every question is searched with the contradicts lens (discontinued, replaced, outage, complaint, settlement) across all source classes. Pass the claim as the question with its subcap_ids and no per-question facet. Fills DQ_Contradicts and the Contradiction_Disposition the ledger demands for an open contradiction; challengers use it to steelman then falsify. Zero cards with coverage.ladder_searched is a recorded failed falsification, not proof the claim holds.

evidence.name: find_corroborating_evidence
evidence.description: Hunts a SECOND, independent source for a claim the run already holds: every question is searched with the corroborates lens across all source classes. Pass the claim as the question with its subcap_ids and no per-question facet. A card from a different origin_cluster (not a syndicated copy) fills DQ_Corroborates and Triangulation, and is what lets a FACT stand on two identities and a vendor (T5) claim rise above its L2 ceiling.

evidence.name: read_entity_newsroom
evidence.description: Evidence cards from the institution's OWN newsroom, press and blog pages (/news, /newsroom, /press, /press-releases, /media, /blog, /insights), sitemap first, robots.txt honoured, page budget and depth capped, with a crawl manifest (seen, fetched, skipped, robots-blocked). The entity's own words: Tier T2 on a disclosure path, T5 where the path is a release (the connector's vendor-collateral cap) — never T1. Dated announcements feed Entity_Timeline; a claim made only here needs a third-party corroboration. Pass `question` to rank pages against a cell question.

evidence.name: read_entity_careers
evidence.description: Evidence cards from the institution's OWN careers pages (open roles, team pages, culture and benefits statements), sitemap first, robots.txt honoured, budget capped, with a crawl manifest. Tier T5 (own site, outside a disclosure path). Roles and required skills are the org_talent and leadership_title proxy classes — what the institution is building and who owns it; a platform named in a role is an INFERENCE. Pass `question` to rank pages against a cell question.

evidence.name: read_entity_investor_pages
evidence.description: Evidence cards from the institution's OWN investor-relations and disclosure pages (annual reports, financial statements, governance, board and committee charters, regulatory disclosures), sitemap first, robots.txt honoured, budget capped, with a crawl manifest. Official disclosure: Tier T2 (never T1 on the own domain), Claim_Type FACT. The source for Firmographics figures (with Unit and As at), governance cells and stated strategy. Pass `question` to rank pages against a cell question.

evidence.name: read_entity_about_pages
evidence.description: Evidence cards from the institution's OWN about, leadership and history pages (who leads it, its charter story, field of membership, locations), sitemap first, robots.txt honoured, budget capped, with a crawl manifest. Tier T5 (own site outside a disclosure path) — leadership names and titles still need a registry or third-party corroboration for the leadership panel. Pass `question` to rank pages against a cell question.

evidence.name: find_sec_filing_evidence
evidence.description: Evidence cards anchored in SEC filings: 10-K, 10-Q and 8-K sections (business, risk factors, MD&A, material events) and XBRL facts with exact values, each card citing the filing URL on sec.gov. Tier T1, Claim_Type FACT — the strongest source a publicly filing institution has. `cik_or_ticker` names the registrant; `forms`, `years` and `topics` narrow the search. A non-SEC filer (most credit unions, private insurers) returns nothing here: use find_regulator_evidence for its call reports and orders instead.

evidence.name: find_registrant
evidence.description: Finds the institution in the REGISTRY that holds it — for all nine sub-verticals in the US and Canada, the first identity step of every run. Pass `entity` {legal_name, aliases[]} and `sub_vertical` (CU, RB, CL, CIB, AM, RIA/WM, IC, IB, FC or its label) and `country` (US or CA; omit for both). Asks, by what the institution is: NCUA (credit unions — charter, type, assets, members, field of membership, HQ, CEO), FDIC BankFind (banks — certificate, primary regulator, assets, HQ), SEC Investment Adviser Public Disclosure and FINRA BrokerCheck (advisers and broker-dealers — CRD, SEC number, status, HQ), the Farm Credit Administration directory (Farm Credit — UNINUM), OSFI (Canadian federally regulated banks, insurers and trusts) and SEC EDGAR (any public or Form D parent — CIK). NAIC and state insurance departments, and Canadian provincial and securities regulators, publish no registry API: they are searched on their own sites and come back as `candidates` (method `search`) to open and confirm, never as a registry record. Every registry asked reports ok, no_match, candidates, error or not_run, and `ambiguous` when two records tie — resolve it with the location before using the identifier.

evidence.name: expand_card_context
evidence.description: The sentences around an evidence card's excerpt, ON DEMAND, from the page the engine cached (`context_handle` from the card's provenance; `window` sentences each side). Use it to disambiguate which institution or product a span is about, for a challenger's check, or a contradiction review — never to lengthen an Excerpt (the registered Excerpt stays the card's verbatim 50–500 character span).

evidence.name: verify_evidence_cards
evidence.description: Re-checks registered evidence cards before they are believed: the URL is still live (or archived), the excerpt is still verbatim at its offsets in the cached page, the item still passes the card contract (Source_Name, Source_URL, Tier, Excerpt length, Claim_Type licence) and the stated Date_Published still parses and is not in the future. Confidence only moves down. Used by the adversarial verifier, the finding challenger, the page consolidator and before promotion.

evidence.name: report_evidence_coverage
evidence.description: The run's evidence coverage, for deciding whether a facet is done: card counts per facet and per label, source diversity, single-source concentration (flag above 40% — a Triangulation risk), the Recency distribution (CURRENT…UNVERIFIED), open conflict candidates, saturation by facet, the evidence-ladder rungs searched (what an absence's Negative_Ladder may cite), and the health of every search backend and upstream search engine.

searxng.name: keyword_search_web_pages
searxng.description: Keyword search of the general web through the run's own SearXNG metasearch (free, keyless engines paced per engine: Google CSE, Bing, Brave, DuckDuckGo, Qwant, mwmbl, Wikipedia). The fallback rung after find_evidence_all_sources: use it for a cell the cards left unanswered, with concise keyword queries (the quoted legal name plus 2–5 content words; `site:<domain>` to stay on one source). `pageno` paginates; `time_range` (day|week|month|year) and `language` narrow.

searxng.name: keyword_search_news
searxng.description: Keyword search of NEWS indexes only (Bing News, DuckDuckGo News, Brave News) through the run's own SearXNG. Use `time_range` (day|week|month|year) to find recent, dated events — launches, partnerships, outages, leadership changes, settlements — for Entity_Timeline and why-now signals. The article's own date, read from the page, is its Date_Published.

searxng.name: keyword_search_papers
searxng.description: Keyword search of SCHOLARLY indexes only (arXiv, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, Crossref) through the run's own SearXNG: papers, working papers and sector studies. Academic sources are Tier T3 and support Why_It_Matters and DMA_Impact, rarely a fact about the entity.

searxng.name: suggest_query_refinements
searxng.description: Autocomplete suggestions for a partial or vague query from the run's SearXNG — the words people actually search with (a product's market name, a programme's public title). Use it to sharpen a query before searching again; it returns no evidence.

searxng.name: check_search_engines
searxng.description: What the run's SearXNG instance can do right now: its categories, the engines configured and enabled, defaults and plugins. Use it to diagnose an empty or thin result list (an engine rested after a CAPTCHA or rate limit) before concluding a source class has nothing; it returns no evidence.

searxng.name: read_web_page_section
searxng.description: Reads ONE web page as markdown, in a bounded way: `readHeadings: true` lists its headings, `section` returns one section by heading, `startChar`/`maxLength` pages through it, `paragraphRange` takes paragraphs. Read the headings first, then only the section that answers the cell question.

fetch.name: read_web_page_markdown
fetch.description: Fetches one URL and returns its content as markdown (`raw` for the original HTML), `max_length` characters from `start_index` — page through a long page instead of reading it whole. Use it for a page a search returned when the evidence engine could not card it (a PDF, a script-rendered page).

edgar.name: get_cik_for_ticker
edgar.description: Converts a stock ticker to the registrant's SEC CIK (Central Index Key), which every other SEC tool accepts as `identifier`. For a name rather than a ticker, find_registrant on the evidence server asks EDGAR and the registry that actually holds the institution.

edgar.name: get_sec_registrant_profile
edgar.description: The registrant's SEC profile: legal name, CIK, SIC industry code, exchange, state of incorporation and fiscal year end — Firmographics registry fields (stated, never held) and the identity anchor for every filing cited.

edgar.name: list_sec_filings
edgar.description: Lists the registrant's recent SEC filings (`form_type` e.g. 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, DEF 14A; `days` back; `limit`) with accession numbers and filing dates — the accession number the section, full-text and 8-K tools need, and the filing date that becomes Date_Published.

edgar.name: read_10k_10q_sections
edgar.description: Extracts named sections — business description, risk factors, MD&A — from one 10-K or 10-Q (`accession_number`, `form_type`). The narrative where strategy, technology investment, cyber and operational risk, and digital initiatives are stated in the registrant's own liable words: verbatim Excerpts for strategy, governance and risk cells.

edgar.name: read_filing_full_text
edgar.description: The full text of one SEC filing, paged (`offset`, `max_chars`) — for an exhibit, a proxy statement (DEF 14A: board, committees, executive officers) or any form the section tool does not cover. Page through it; take one verbatim span per claim.

edgar.name: read_8k_material_events
edgar.description: The material events one 8-K reports, by item: 1.01 material agreements (a platform or vendor contract), 2.02 results, 5.02 officer and director changes (leadership panel), 7.01 Regulation FD disclosures, 8.01 other events. Dated events for Entity_Timeline and why-now signals.

edgar.name: get_financial_statements
edgar.description: The registrant's financial statements from its filings (`statement_type`: all, income, balance or cash) — revenue, assets, deposits, expenses — for the financial trajectory and Firmographics (each figure with its Unit and As at period).

edgar.name: get_key_financial_metrics
edgar.description: Named key metrics from the registrant's XBRL data (`metrics`, e.g. Revenues, Assets, NetIncomeLoss) as reported values with their periods — the figures behind a CAGR candidate (serve one only when an independent source corroborates it).

edgar.name: get_business_segment_data
edgar.description: Revenue and results by reported segment (`segment_type`: geographic or business) — which lines of business the registrant reports, for the LOB census and subsidiary or segment Firmographics (admissible when the unit names the entity).

edgar.name: compare_financial_periods
edgar.description: One metric across a span of fiscal years (`metric`, `start_year`, `end_year`) with the change between them — the reported series a growth figure or trajectory is computed from.

edgar.name: get_xbrl_company_facts
edgar.description: Every XBRL fact the registrant has reported across its filings, by concept and period — the complete reported record when a named metric is not enough.

edgar.name: list_reported_metrics
edgar.description: Which XBRL metrics the registrant actually reports, with data counts (`search_term` filters by name) — run it before get_key_financial_metrics so a metric is asked for by the concept the registrant uses.

edgar.name: list_xbrl_concepts
edgar.description: Every XBRL concept present in one filing (`accession_number`, or the latest `form_type`; `namespace_filter` e.g. us-gaap), with sample values — run it before get_xbrl_filing_concepts.

edgar.name: get_xbrl_filing_concepts
edgar.description: Specific XBRL concept values from one filing (`concepts`, `accession_number` or the latest `form_type`) — an exact reported figure with its period, cited to that filing.
